title: Harvest and Portrait
premise: Freya Nystrom takes a teaching post in the isolated village of Vessing, where eleven students have vanished over a century and every record of them has been erased. When the church bell—melted down in 1911—begins ringing at dawn, Freya's obsessive documentation becomes the only thread connecting the missing to the living. She discovers the founders bound the village's prosperity to an unfinished harvest ritual that requires a 'portrait' of souls: names written and then surrendered. To save her current class from being collected, Freya must complete the ritual herself, inscribing her own name last—and in doing so, she vanishes into the village's memory while the children she saved grow old remembering a teacher no record can prove existed.
about_author: Yara Dunmore is the pen name of a former rural schoolteacher who spent nine years in northern farming communities before turning to writing full-time. Her fiction draws on parish archives, folk hymnals, and the particular loneliness of small schools.

chapters.title: The Long Road to Vessing
chapters.summary: Freya arrives by bus through fog-choked farmland, cataloguing everything in her notebook as a coping ritual. The village feels welcoming but rehearsed, like actors awaiting a cue. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: cautious hope shadowed by the sense of being watched.

chapters.title: Eleven Desks
chapters.summary: On her first day, Freya counts twelve students but finds thirteen desks, one older than the rest and never used. Headmaster Aldous Vey deflects her questions with practiced charm. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: unease taking root beneath professional optimism.

chapters.title: What the Register Doesn't Say
chapters.summary: Digging through school records, Freya finds gaps—years where students simply stop appearing mid-term, no transfers, no deaths recorded. The janitor, old Marta, warns her to stop counting. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: the thrill of discovery curdling into dread.

chapters.title: A Bell That Isn't There
chapters.summary: At dawn the whole village wakes to bell-ringing; the church tower has been empty since the original bell was melted for the war effort in 1911. Villagers act unsurprised. POV: Freya, with a brief interlude from student Tomas. Emotional beat: collective denial pressing against one witness.

chapters.title: The Founders' Ledger
chapters.summary: In the sealed vestry archive, Freya finds the founders' ledger: a harvest covenant promising abundance in exchange for 'portraits'—written names surrendered at each bell-season. Eleven names are listed; the twelfth line is blank. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: horror of understanding the arithmetic.

chapters.title: Tomas Hears It Too
chapters.summary: Student Tomas admits he hears his missing sister's voice inside the bell-sound. Freya realizes the children are more attuned than the adults. POV: Tomas, framed by Freya's notes. Emotional beat: tenderness and terror entwined—the first real alliance.

chapters.title: Portrait Day
chapters.summary: The school holds its annual Portrait Day, where every child's name is written on vellum and hung in the church—a tradition Freya now recognizes as the ritual's harvesting mechanism. She secretly copies the vellum list. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: complicity; she has participated without knowing.

chapters.title: Marta's Confession
chapters.summary: The janitor reveals she was a child when the last collection happened in 1963; she survived because her mother scratched her name off the vellum and paid for it with her own. Marta begs Freya to leave. POV: Marta. Emotional beat: grief worn smooth by decades of silence.

chapters.title: Invisible Was Never Safe
chapters.summary: Freya attempts to report the disappearances to authorities in the nearest town, but every official she contacts turns out to have Vessing roots—or no record at all. The village's reach is older than law. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: isolation; justice outside the system is the only kind left.

chapters.title: The Twelfth Line
chapters.summary: Freya deciphers the ledger's final instruction: the covenant remains unfinished until a twelfth name is freely given, completing the portrait and ending the collections forever—or beginning them eternally. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: the trap revealed—refusal feeds it too.

chapters.title: Vey's Bargain
chapters.summary: Headmaster Vey confesses his family has kept the ledger for generations; his own son was taken in 1989 because he hesitated. He offers Freya a way out: write any name but her own. POV: Vey. Emotional beat: moral vertigo—survival offered at someone else's cost.

chapters.title: What the Children Know
chapters.summary: Freya's students, sensing the season turning, present her with their own research: drawings of the vanished, matched to faces in century-old photographs. The missing don't die—they persist inside the bell's sound. POV: ensemble, anchored by student Ingrid. Emotional beat: children's clarity shaming adult cowardice.

chapters.title: Bell-Season Begins
chapters.summary: Autumn deepens; the bell rings nightly now, closer each time, and frost forms in the shape of names on classroom windows. One student, Petra, stops speaking entirely. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: countdown pressure; the village's warmth turns watchful.

chapters.title: The Harvest of Names
chapters.summary: Freya experiments with false names on spare vellum; each burns to ash by morning, and something scratches at her door in response. The ritual cannot be cheated, only completed or refused. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: the closing of escape routes.

chapters.title: Marta's Grave
chapters.summary: Freya visits the unmarked grave of Marta's mother and finds the scratched-out name still faintly legible—proof a name removed can free a soul, but only if given back willingly by another. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: fragile hope built on an old sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Village Decides
chapters.summary: At a town meeting, villagers vote—not unanimously—to let the season take a child rather than risk the covenant breaking and the land failing. Freya watches neighbors she liked choose sacrifice. POV: Freya with interludes from dissenters. Emotional beat: righteous fury; belonging revealed as predation.

chapters.title: Petra Speaks
chapters.summary: Petra breaks her silence: the voices in the bell told her the missing want to come home, and they need a living hand to finish the portrait honestly. Freya understands the ritual can be turned. POV: Petra. Emotional beat: the dead become allies, not threats.

chapters.title: Stealing the Vellum
chapters.summary: Freya, Tomas, and Ingrid break into the church on the eve of the final bell to steal the Portrait Day vellum containing the children's names. Vey catches them—and instead of stopping them, hands over the founders' ledger. POV: Tomas. Emotional beat: betrayal inverted into aid; even the keeper defects.

chapters.title: The Unfinished Ritual
chapters.summary: In the belfry that holds no bell, Freya begins the completion rite: reading the eleven stolen names aloud to call the missing home, each returning name shaking the empty tower like a struck bell. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: terrible beauty; the dead pouring back toward the living.

chapters.title: The Twelfth Name
chapters.summary: The ritual demands its final entry. Freya writes her own name, refusing Vey's earlier bargain and every easy alternative, and the covenant accepts—her body thinning into sound as the eleventh missing child steps out of the air. POV: Freya, dissolving. Emotional beat: willing sacrifice as the only just verdict.

chapters.title: After the Ringing
chapters.summary: The bell falls silent forever; the vanished return aged as if no time passed, and the village must reckon with what it voted to allow. Vey burns the ledger publicly. POV: Marta and Tomas. Emotional beat: raw accountability—justice done, but not comfortably.

chapters.title: A Teacher No Record Proves
chapters.summary: Years later, the returned students—now grown—keep an empty thirteenth desk in every classroom and tell their own children about Miss Nystrom, though no document confirms she ever existed. On quiet dawns, some swear they hear chalk on a board. POV: Ingrid, adult. Emotional beat: mourning transmuted into belonging; memory as the truest register.
